scope: The drawer's differences from the dialog (side variant, data-swipe-direction, swipe to dismiss) in happy-dom: the headless swipe (dom/swipe.ts), the web component and the React renderer (server markup, client swipe); the shared dialog behavior is covered by the dialog's record. Rendered lengths are covered by the browser geometry check and the React parity check; visual quality and screen-reader output are not certified.

checks.covers: swipe: slop, movement variables, no movement away from the edge, threshold, spring back, data-swipe-dismiss and reset, [data-swipe-ignore], cross-axis drags; element: side variant classes and data-swipe-direction (unknown side = bottom), modal, swipe and outside-press reasons, no native form elements
resolveDrawer: panel padding inside B, square at any corner scale, 2u gap, 80u side width within the 8u reserve, full-width top and bottom sheets
React SSR: the same data-* as the web component, side variant classes, data-swipe-direction, composed parts = preset; client: a swipe calls onOpenChange(false, { reason: 'swipe' })

limitations: The slide transition and real pointer capture need a real browser: a Playwright drag in Chromium (2026-11-02) moved the sheet with the pointer (data-swiping, --drawer-swipe-movement-x), sprang back after 60px and closed with reason swipe after 220px of a 360px sheet, lifting the page's inert.
React styling parity is checked in the browser: apps/studio/react-check.html ("fails": []), the open sheets compared part by part.

Geometry review, manual items (2026-11-02, studio on the Components page Overlays family at u = 3, the theme unit 4.5 and 6, light and dark): growth (a tall bottom sheet stops at the viewport height less 8u and scrolls; a narrow viewport narrows a side sheet to the viewport less 8u; actions wrap), RTL (sides are physical by design: side=left stays left, the content inside mirrors), focus (rings are outlines and change no dimension; focus is trapped and returns to the trigger), screenshots of the right and bottom sheets checked light and dark.
